surfaces.part: flat roof with parapet (gravel roof deck)

answer.evidence: The roof deck is a large textured brown-grey surface running from the parapet at rows 3-4 down to row 41, so it is foreshortened but clearly visible from above. It ends in a pale front cornice band at rows 42-45 with a darker edge line at row 46. The stairwell head box has a pale top at rows 6-13 and a front face with a dark door at rows 14-23, ending in a dark shadow line at row 24. The south front face runs from row 42 to the bottom of the sprite (about 70 rows) and holds four rows of windows plus balconies with visible slab tops. No receding side face is drawn.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a whole building, so the comparison is valid. Measured facts: 15 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10 for the references, 6% near-flat coverage against 0%, and only 1% of dark edge pixels near-neutral, so the outline is tinted. Outlines look like dark grey-blue concrete tones, with the windows and balconies set apart by value rather than a uniform black line. The concrete wall and roof show speckle, cracks, rubble, ivy and stains, giving about 5 steps on the main ramp. The reference roofs and walls show per-tile scallops and timber grain across 6 steps. The candidate's concrete is a little more uniform and its window rows repeat, so it reads slightly less crafted than the references, but it is not a flat sticker. Overall it is acceptable beside the references.
